summary.text: Case 1, an 81-year-old woman with dementia, BMI 20.1 kg/m² and uCCI 2, had type III hiatal hernia and preoperative dysphagia score 3, with grade N endoscopy and no reflux esophagitis. She underwent laparoscopic hiatal repair and anterior gastropexy without fundoplication, using five ports, posterior nonabsorbable hiatal sutures, flexible endoscopic GEJ calibration and two 2–0 Prolene anterior fixation sutures. Operative duration was 249 minutes and Table 1 blood loss 13 mL. Table 1 listed no immediate postoperative complication. Postoperative stay was 8 days. Postoperative grade A reflux esophagitis and temporary heartburn were treatable with unspecified medication; prolonged heartburn and temporary/prolonged dysphagia were absent. Authors report improved dysphagia scores and favorable FSSG response; individual numeric FSSG values are not supplied in text and exact follow-up durations are unreported. Individual Table 1 blood-loss and stay claims are retained despite inconsistent pooled summaries; no pooled statistic is assigned to this patient.

summary.text: Case 3, an 86-year-old woman with dementia, BMI 26.3 kg/m² and uCCI 2, had type III hiatal hernia and preoperative dysphagia score 4, with grade N endoscopy and no reflux esophagitis. She underwent laparoscopic hiatal repair and anterior gastropexy without fundoplication, using five ports, posterior nonabsorbable hiatal sutures, flexible endoscopic GEJ calibration and two 2–0 Prolene anterior fixation sutures. Operative duration was 168 minutes and Table 1 blood loss 0 mL. Delayed gastric emptying complicated the postoperative course. Postoperative stay was 10 days. Postoperative recurrence was documented on endoscopy/CT, with the single recurrent hernia described as type I. She had neither temporary/prolonged heartburn nor temporary/prolonged dysphagia and was on unspecified medication. Authors report improved dysphagia scores and favorable FSSG response; individual numeric FSSG values are not supplied in text and exact follow-up durations are unreported. Individual Table 1 blood-loss and stay claims are retained despite inconsistent pooled summaries; no pooled statistic is assigned to this patient.
